items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: I played with the Olinca band... He had a Henry Julian on saxophone.

ctx.x: Was he playing clarinet then or saxophone? He said clarinet. When did he take up saxophone, do you know? No, I don't. Well, what was the next band after that that you played with?

I played with the Olinca band. He had an eight-piece band. As I know, the pass on drum and the album of Tablet, trumpet. He had a Henry Julian on saxophone. Is that a sax and clarinet? Yeah. It used, yeah, we used two trumpets, sax and clarinet, made of eight pieces. No trombone? Yeah, one trombone, bass and a banjo. What would he have on saxophone? Sometimes it would be Hoybert Moran, different fellas. For a while he had whatever it was Moran.
So many of them. Yeah. Did they play from sheet music? It's a big band. Well, yeah.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: that taught Henry Julian... Well, that was Henry Julian's grandfather. He was a saxophone player with the Olympic Band. And when I joined the Olympic Band, well, he got me to go to his grandfather for lessons.

ctx.x: Is he still here? He's the one
that taught Henry Julian. You ever heard of Henry Julian?
